## Probe built and pushed (Gerrit 1359). Two process constraints hit, both recorded.

`scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py` + `.github/workflows/jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml`: plain deterministic urllib, four predetermined REST calls, **no LLM and no agent**, so it cannot re-run or churn the committed capability map. Three parity guards assert that separation in `test_jira_dc_capability_map_workflow.py` — dispatch-only, read-only permissions, and explicitly that the workflow neither invokes `jira_dc_capability_map.py` nor carries an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. It runs in CI because the harness image is linux/amd64-only.

### Constraint 1 — it cannot be dispatched until it LANDS

`gh workflow run --ref probe/epic-link-clear` fails:

    HTTP 404: workflow jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml not found on the default branch

GitHub only dispatches `workflow_dispatch` files that exist on the DEFAULT branch, so unlike a harness run (which reuses an already-landed workflow on a topic branch) this probe must merge to `main` first. That is a real sequencing cost for any NEW workflow and worth knowing before designing the next one.

### Constraint 2 — my own process miss

1359 drew `LLM-Review -1`, sole finding `bugfix-size-attestation`: 289 non-test lines with no plan-review attestation on this bug. AGENTS.md prescribes exactly this for a fix whose blast radius reaches non-test code — declare `file_impact`, write the plan into the description, run `review-plan` BEFORE implementing — and I went straight to writing the probe. Corrected: `file_impact` now declares all three paths with reasons, and `review-plan` returned **PASS with zero blocking**. Recheck posted.

The finding was correct and the gate did its job; the sequence was mine to get right.

## PROBE-4B9E-R1: the probe ran, FAILED AT SETUP, and destroyed its own evidence

Run 30930839323, `main` @ 40a0efad8. **No verdict recorded. The blocking unknown is still open, so
the Rank 1 cell stays unwritten** — which is the discipline this ticket set for itself.

### What the run said, in full

```
PROBE SETUP FAILED: Epic Link=None Epic Name=None
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
##[error]No files were found with the provided path: .../jira-dc-epic-link-probe
```

That is the entire diagnostic surface. Jira booted (the step started ~10 min into the run and
answered in 1.4s), so this is not a readiness timeout.

### The defect that made it undiagnosable — and the more useful finding

Evidence was written only AFTER the last question, and every `PROBE SETUP FAILED` path raises
`SystemExit`. So the one artifact built to explain a failure was the one artifact guaranteed to be
discarded exactly when it was needed, and the upload step then failed for having nothing to upload.

**On an amd64-only image every attempt costs a full boot cycle, so an undiagnosable failure is the
expensive failure.** I built the probe to answer a question and did not build it to survive not
answering it. Fixed in Gerrit 1373:

* evidence is written on ANY exit — clean, `SystemExit`, or unexpected exception;
* discovery reports WHY: the HTTP status and body type when `/rest/api/2/field` is unusable, or the
  inventory size plus the names actually present when the field is genuinely absent. A bare `None`
  conflated "instance unreachable/unauthorised" with "field does not exist";
* `Accept: application/json` is now sent, matching `conftest._request` and
  `test_dc_mutations._admin_request`. The probe sent only `Content-Type`, and it is the one caller
  in this family that omitted `Accept` — a plausible cause of a non-list body, though NOT yet
  demonstrated as the cause, and I am not recording a diagnosis I have not measured.

### Why the field is probably not actually missing

`_named_field_id` in the live mutation suite resolves "Epic Link" against the same image by the same
name-match over `/rest/api/2/field`, and the capability map measured WRITING the Epic Link
(req-0040/0041). So an inventory genuinely lacking the field would contradict two prior
measurements. That is a reason to instrument rather than a reason to conclude — the next run's
evidence decides it.

### CONSTRAINT 1, REFINED — worth carrying forward

My earlier note said a new `workflow_dispatch` workflow "cannot be dispatched until it lands". The
precise rule is narrower and more useful: the workflow FILE must exist on the DEFAULT branch to be
dispatchable at all, but once it does, `--ref` may target any ref that GitHub can see, and the run
then executes THAT ref's workflow and scripts. So the landing cost is paid once per workflow, not
once per iteration of the script it runs.

## PROBE-4B9E-R2: ROOT CAUSE FOUND. `serverInfo` 200 is NOT readiness for Jira Software custom fields.

Run 30944211742, `main` @ b868ea914. Still `PROBE SETUP FAILED: Epic Link=None Epic Name=None` — but
this time the evidence survived, which is exactly what Gerrit 1373 was for. **One run, from
undiagnosable to diagnosed.**

### The diagnostic the fix added

```
field 'Epic Link' absent from an inventory of 27 field(s); names present:
  ['Archived','Archiver','Attachment','Comment','Created','Creator','Images','Key','Last Viewed',
   'Log Work','Original Estimate','Progress','Project','Remaining Estimate','Resolved','Status',
   'Sub-Tasks','Time Spent','Time Tracking','Updated','Votes','Watchers','Work Ratio',
   'Σ Original Estimate','Σ Progress','Σ Remaining Estimate','Σ Time Spent']
ABORTED — wrote 2 recorded round trip(s) to .../evidence.json before exiting
```

The inventory is **27 fields and every one is a SYSTEM field.** Not one `customfield_*`. So the field
list was readable and authorised — the request worked fine — and Jira Software's GreenHopper fields
(`Epic Link`, `Epic Name`) simply **had not been registered yet**. My earlier hypothesis that a missing
`Accept` header was producing a non-list body was wrong; the body was a perfectly good list of the
wrong contents.

### The timing proves it

```
Wait for Jira DC to become ready : 19:39:01 -> 19:47:33   (8m32s, polling /rest/api/2/serverInfo)
Run the Epic-Link clear probe    : 19:47:33 -> 19:47:34   (1 SECOND later)
```

`serverInfo` answered 200 after 8m32s; **one second later** the custom fields were still absent.

### Why the harness never hit this, and why that is its own latent bug

Both workflows use the IDENTICAL readiness gate — `.github/workflows/jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml:50-60`
and `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml:526-536` both poll `serverInfo` until 200. The harness
is not more careful; it is just SLOWER afterwards. It installs dependencies and then runs a 41-minute
suite, so by the time `conftest._assert_project_capabilities` checks for `Epic Link` / `Epic Name`,
minutes have passed and the plugin is up. The probe queries in the first second and sees the truth.

**So the harness's declared-environment contract (bug 3fe5) is asserted against a readiness signal too
weak to guarantee it.** If a future run reached that fixture faster, or the plugin initialised slower,
`_assert_project_capabilities` would fail at provisioning and report it as the 3fe5 image degrade —
"the image no longer yields the declared environment" — when the real cause is timing. That is a
misattributing flake waiting to happen, and it is the same family as 3fe5 itself: a contract checked at
the wrong moment. Filed separately.

### The fix for this probe

Wait for the CAPABILITY the probe actually needs, not a proxy for it: poll `/rest/api/2/field` until
`Epic Link` appears, under its own bounded budget, and fail with the inventory dump if it never does.
`serverInfo` is the wrong predicate for anything that depends on a plugin's fields.

**4b9e's blocking unknown is STILL UNANSWERED** — whether `{epic_link_field_id: None}` actually clears
on DC 8.17.1. The Rank 1 cell stays unwritten. But the obstacle is now a known, small, fixable
readiness bug rather than a mystery, and each attempt no longer costs a blind boot cycle.

## The BLOCKING UNKNOWN is already answered — by the harness, green, in run 30951453979

This ticket held the Rank 1 cell unwritten pending a probe of whether `{epic_link: null}` actually
clears on DC 8.17.1. **It does, and the evidence was already in the suite.** Two cells PASSED in
live run `30951453979` (`main` @ d394a70529):

* **`test_outbound_epic_parent_round_trips_via_the_epic_link`** — its final two statements are
  literally `dc_transport.set_parent(child, None)` followed by a raw-REST read and
  `assert not cleared`. That IS the probe's question, asserted, green.
* **`test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips`** — an Epic Link clear observed arriving INBOUND
  through `get_parent_map`'s Epic Link fallback (9bb9).

`scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py` was answering a question two green cells had already
answered. Both PROBE-4B9E-R1 and R2 burned a full amd64 boot cycle on a question the harness had
settled. **Worth generalising: before building a probe, check whether an existing green cell already
asserts the thing.** The probe still earns its keep as a fast deterministic re-check, and R2's real
finding — that `serverInfo` 200 is NOT readiness for Jira Software custom fields — stands on its own
and is a latent hazard for any new workflow.

Recorded in `docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md` with the run id, so the next reader finds it.

## The AC branch that decided the work is therefore settled

> "if it does NOT clear: that is a product defect — file it, and add the missing read-back"

**Not triggered.** It clears. The Rank 1 re-home is unblocked and is what this change delivers.

## Why the cell was ACTUALLY red — a different mechanism from the other two reds

Run `30951453979`: `AssertionError` — "the local parent was DETACHED but `RBJUFQU-2` still carries
`fields.parent = RBJUFQU-1`". Of the three candidates the cell's own message lists, it is the third:
the clear IS emitted (a locally detached ticket takes `_resolve_local_parent`'s `(True, None)`
branch at `outbound_field_diff.py:145` — bug 8b25's non-epic guard is NOT implicated), `set_parent`
writes `{"parent": None}` for a sub-task (`_hierarchy.py:169`), DC answers **400** (`req-0055`), and
`dispatch_one` swallows it with a warning. Pass exits 0, remote parent survives.

This ticket's own reading of the managed-ref gate was nonetheless CORRECT and is load-bearing for
the re-home: `_parent_clear_is_managed` -> `should_propagate_removal` fires only for a ref in
`managed_refs`, and a local `edit_ticket(..., parent=...)` is what folds it in
(`reducer/_processors.py:528`). Priming the parent by CREATING the issue under it Jira-side — what
the old cell did — does not reliably establish rebar as the manager. The re-homed cell primes
through a local edit carried by a real pass, and proves that attach landed before asking for the
clear.

## The cell was also self-contradicted inside its own file

`test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips` ends with 37e7's pin asserting `pytest.raises(Exception)` on
exactly `set_parent(subtask_child, None)`. This cell asserted the same call succeeds end-to-end. One
of the two had to be red; 37e7's operator ruling makes it this one.

## SCOPE CHANGE, flagged rather than absorbed

This ticket's AC says `test_outbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` becomes `xfail(strict=True)`.
**The operator's 2026-08-04 ruling for [rebar:9f26-66c2-14af-4223] forbids xfail** ("resolve the
failures, don't remove the tests"), so that AC is superseded. That cell is instead re-homed under
9f26 to the claim nothing currently asserts — that an unrepresentable parent must produce a durable
bridge alert rather than being silently dropped — which is a stronger outcome than an xfail: it
turns a permanent red into a green assertion about behaviour rebar actually owns.

## Also worth recording: the non-sub-task read-back gap this ticket identified is REAL

`set_parent`'s Epic Link branch (`_hierarchy.py:147-168`) still has **no read-back verification**,
unlike the sub-task branch 1a9f hardened. It is not currently masking anything — the Epic Link
round-trips green in both directions — so adding it is hardening rather than a fix, and it is left
out of this change to keep the diff narrow. Flagged here so it is a decision rather than an
oversight.

## Gerrit **1400** pushed — test-only, and the probe turned out to be unnecessary

Stacked on **1399** (9f26). One file: `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py`, no
production code.

### What changed in the cell

`test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips` now clears an **Epic Link on a standard-issue child**
instead of `fields.parent` on a sub-task. This ticket's own analysis of the managed-ref gate was
**correct and is load-bearing**: `_parent_clear_is_managed` -> `should_propagate_removal` fires
only for a ref in `managed_refs`, and `reducer/_processors.py:528` folds it in on a local
`edit_ticket(..., parent=...)`. So the cell primes the parent through a LOCAL rebar edit carried
by a real pass — not by creating the issue under a parent Jira-side, which is what the old cell
did and what left the ref unmanaged.

Assertion count went **7 -> 10**. No skip, no xfail, no loosened round trip.

### A vacuous-green bug in my own first draft, caught in review

My first version ended with `assert not after` on the Epic Link **without checking the HTTP
status**. A 401/403/500 returns a dict like `{"errorMessages": [...]}`, whose `.get("fields")`
is None — so `after` was falsy and **the cell would have gone GREEN on a failed read**. Now
asserts `status == 200 and isinstance(body, dict) and "fields" in body` first. The positive
assertions above it (comparing against an expected key) are safe without that; a
**must-be-absent** oracle never is. Worth generalising: every "assert X is gone" oracle in this
suite needs the read proven successful first.

### The probe: keep it, but the question it was built for is settled

`scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py` and its workflow are untouched and still land. But two
green cells in run 30951453979 already answered its question, so it was not on the critical path.
The R2 finding it produced — **`serverInfo` 200 is NOT readiness for Jira Software custom
fields** — stands on its own and is a latent hazard for any new workflow using that gate.

### AC status

- [x] the probe's verdict question — **ANSWERED: it clears** (via the harness, not the probe)
- [ ] the re-home is written and lints clean; **needs a live run to confirm green** (run id to be
      recorded here)
- [n/a] the "if it does NOT clear" branch — not triggered
- [superseded] the `xfail(strict=True)` AC — the operator ruling on [rebar:9f26-66c2-14af-4223]
      forbids xfail; that cell is re-homed under 9f26 instead
- [x] no cell weakened

Gates: `make lint` **0**, `make typecheck` **0**, marker-selected suite **0** (10202 passed).
**Not closing** — needs the harness run.

compiled_state.description:
# Re-home the outbound parent-CLEAR live cell to the Epic Link path

`test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips` is one of three permanent reds in the live DC suite. It
clears a **sub-task's** `fields.parent`, which Data Center will not do. Its INBOUND twin was
already re-homed to the Epic Link by ticket 37e7's approved ruling; the outbound twin never was.

## The three reds are three DIFFERENT problems, not one

That reframing is the finding — treating them as one platform limitation is what kept them
together in red.

| cell | real blocker | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips` | the cell picked a sub-task; the Epic Link path is reachable | **this ticket** |
| `test_outbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` | rebar must do the write and DC accepts-and-ignores it — unreachable, and its coverage is already green elsewhere | `xfail(strict=True)` |
| `test_inbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` | the DC-side reparent is only SETUP; the subject is rebar's inbound pass | re-target to adoption |

The outbound-set behaviour rebar can actually deliver is already pinned green by
`test_a_subtask_reparent_is_REFUSED_rather_than_silently_ignored`, so `xfail(strict=True)` there
loses no coverage — and an xpass would FAIL the suite, a stronger signal than today's permanent
red.

## Why the Epic Link clear is believed reachable (source-verified)

 * `_resolve_local_parent` returns `(True, None)` for a locally-detached ticket regardless of
   parent type — the epic-only guard suppresses *sets*, not *clears*.
 * `fetcher.merge_parent_map` overlays `client.get_parent_map()`, and 9bb9 taught DC's
   `get_parent_map` to fall back to the Epic Link — so a standard issue under an epic yields a
   truthy `remote_parent_id` and the clear is observable outbound.
 * `set_parent` for a non-sub-task writes `{epic_link_field_id: None}` — the same path as a set.

Two gates the cell must be built around, or it will fail for the wrong reason:
 1. `should_propagate_removal` requires the ref to be MANAGED — so the cell must have **rebar**
    set the Epic Link in a priming pass, not create it Jira-side.
 2. `_peer_removed_the_parent` (339a) short-circuits on a truthy remote parent, so it does not
    interfere.

## THE BLOCKING UNKNOWN

**Whether `{epic_link_field_id: None}` actually clears on DC 8.17.1 is UNTESTED.** The capability
map measured that WRITING the Epic Link works (req-0040/0041); clearing it was never probed. Do
not write the cell before this is answered — that is exactly how changes 1276, 1288 and 1302 each
shipped merged, mutation-proven and wrong.

A targeted, deterministic probe is added by this ticket:
`scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py` + `.github/workflows/jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml`.
It is NOT the capability map — no LLM, no agent, four predetermined REST calls — so it settles
the question without re-running or churning the map's committed answers.

## A related gap this surfaced

`set_parent`'s **non-sub-task branch has no read-back verification**, unlike the sub-task branch
that 1a9f added. If the Epic Link clear silently no-ops, that is invisible today. Worth closing
regardless of the probe's answer, though the probe's result decides whether adding it makes
`set_parent` start refusing epic-parent clears (correct, and the same move 1a9f made).

## Ruled out, with evidence — do not re-investigate

 * **screen provisioning for `parent`** — REFUTED. `OrderableField` is defined as "fields able to
   be placed on screens" and Jira Server 8.x has NO Parent implementation of it; `parent` is
   absent from `/rest/api/2/field` (JRASERVER-47377, closed unfixed). It cannot be screened. This
   does not contradict the map's screen-gating finding, which was about a field that EXISTS.
 * **sub-task ⟷ standard conversion via REST** — no such endpoint in the 8.17.0 reference
   (JRASERVER-27893 open since 2012; the adjacent issuetype-change request closed Won't Do).
 * **bulk edit / `/issue/move` / `overrideScreenSecurity`** — none exist on DC 8.x
   (`/subtask/move` is sibling REORDERING); `overrideScreenSecurity` occurs zero times in the
   8.17/8.22/9.4/9.12 references — Cloud-and-app-only.
 * **delete-and-recreate** — rejected: new key, lost history, and a broken binding.

## STATUS UPDATE (2026-08-04) — the blocking unknown is ANSWERED and one AC is SUPERSEDED

**The probe is no longer needed to proceed.** Two cells that PASSED in live run `30951453979`
already answer whether `{epic_link: null}` clears on DC:
`test_outbound_epic_parent_round_trips_via_the_epic_link` (whose final assertion is
`set_parent(child, None)` then `assert not cleared`) and `test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips`.
**It clears.** So AC2 is the live branch and AC3's "if it does NOT clear" branch is moot. Recorded
in `docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md` with the run id.

**AC4 (xfail) is SUPERSEDED by the operator ruling on [rebar:9f26-66c2-14af-4223] (2026-08-04):**
"resolve the failures; do NOT delete, skip, or `xfail` any cell."
`test_outbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` is therefore NOT xfailed — it is re-homed under
9f26 to the claim nothing currently asserts (an unrepresentable parent must produce a durable
bridge alert rather than being silently dropped). That is a stronger outcome than an xfail: a
permanent red becomes a green assertion about behaviour rebar owns.

**Scope of this ticket is now test-only:** re-home `test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips` to the
Epic Link clear, priming the parent through a LOCAL rebar edit so `should_propagate_removal` sees a
MANAGED ref. The `set_parent` non-sub-task read-back gap this ticket correctly identified is real
but is NOT currently masking anything (the Epic Link round-trips green in both directions), so it
is left out to keep the diff narrow — a recorded decision, not an oversight.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the probe runs in CI and its verdict on `{epic_link: null}` is recorded here
- [x] if it CLEARS: `test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips` is re-homed to the Epic Link path
      (rebar-set parent in a priming pass) and is GREEN on a live run, with the run id recorded
- [x] if it does NOT clear: that is a product defect — file it, and add the missing read-back to
      `set_parent`'s non-sub-task branch so it stops reporting a no-op as success
- [x] `test_outbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` is `xfail(strict=True)` with a reason citing
      the measured platform limitation
- [x] no cell is weakened to pass — no skips, no deleted assertions, no round-trip loosened
